title: Associations between features and sample metadata
summary: Fits per-feature models across a cohort and reports which features associate with the supplied fixed effects, in both abundance and prevalence. Runs once over the whole cohort, not per sample.

third_party.name: maaslin3
third_party.note: Carries the entire computation. The file above assembles arguments and calls it, so the package version is the scientific surface. Its own normalization and its own multiple-testing correction are inside it and are not ours.

third_party.name: lme4
third_party.note: Supplies the mixed model used whenever a random effect is given.

environment.provenance: No image. Runs as a subprocess inside an renv project pinning 295 packages, declared through environment.activation.

activation.note: renv project. Its .Rprofile puts the 295 pinned packages on the library path, and only does so when R starts inside this directory.

inputs.name: features
inputs.description: Samples by features, sample_id in the first column. Raw abundances: maaslin3 does its own normalization and transform.

inputs.name: metadata
inputs.description: Samples by variables, same sample_id index, carrying every fixed and random effect named below.

outputs.name: all_results
outputs.description: Every feature-by-effect model fit, significant or not.

outputs.name: significant_results
outputs.description: The subset passing max_significance, by the package's own correction.

parameters.name: fixed_effects
parameters.description: Metadata columns tested for association. STRAIN: this is required in practice — the capability is meaningless without it — but the format has no way to say a parameter is mandatory, only that an input is.

parameters.name: random_effects
parameters.description: Grouping columns for repeated measures, e.g. subject_id. Absent, every sample is treated as independent.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Reference level for a categorical fixed effect, as 'variable,level'. Changes what every coefficient is relative to.

parameters.name: normalization
parameters.description: Package normalization applied before the transform.

parameters.name: min_prevalence
parameters.description: Features present in fewer than this fraction of samples are dropped before fitting, which also shrinks the multiple-testing family.

parameters.name: min_abundance
parameters.description: Abundance floor for the prevalence test above.

parameters.name: max_significance
parameters.description: Cutoff for the significant_results table. This is the package's own corrected value, not an FDR we compute.

determinism.note: UNVERIFIED. The models are fitted rather than sampled, so runs are expected to be reproducible without a seed. Not measured here.

resources.memory_hint: One model per feature per effect, parallel across features. Not measured here.

notes: First entry written for this domain. The kernel is the R wrapper; the argument assembly that used to sit in Python is this file.
for_people: Tests which features are associated with sample metadata, allowing for repeated sampling.
